dashboard_trackers.name: IRAN NUCLEAR
dashboard_trackers.notes: The official IAEA Iran Board-report index still shows GOV/2026/33 dated 4 Jun as the newest safeguards report. No fresh evidence of 90% enrichment, a nuclear test, Fordow activation or restored/denied access threshold surfaced; raw/coupled risk holds 56/64

dashboard_trackers.name: IRAN WAR
dashboard_trackers.notes: Reuters reports the proposed Iran-Oman Hormuz framework remains under negotiation but four shipping/insurance sources call it unworkable under U.S. sanctions and Lloyd’s war-cover clauses. Iran seeks 5–7% cargo-value fees, while a preliminary parliamentary bill would bar U.S., Israeli and other “hostile” ships and impose fines up to 20%. Transit remains severely constrained; diplomacy_active, hormuz_controlled_not_closed, hormuz_mining and oil_infrastructure_threat persist. Raw/coupled risk holds 95/100

dashboard_trackers.name: ISRAEL-LEBANON
dashboard_trackers.notes: Reuters reports two Israeli soldiers killed and four wounded by an explosive device during a southern-Lebanon sweep; Israeli retaliation killed one Lebanese person and wounded 12. Rome talks continued, and Israel's defence minister omitted a new Hezbollah attribution in his mourning statement, suggesting no wider retaliatory step yet. Existing ceasefire_violation, diplomacy_active and diplomacy_refused signals persist; raw/coupled risk holds 95/100

dashboard_trackers.name: TURKEY-NATO
dashboard_trackers.notes: Past-24h wire, NATO and regional review found no direct Türkiye combat threshold, official nuclear rhetoric or qualifying missile-range test. A draft PKK reintegration law is political context, not a configured escalation signal; risk holds 5/deterrent

dashboard_trackers.name: INDIA-PAKISTAN
dashboard_trackers.notes: Past-24h review found no independently corroborated India-Pakistan force buildup or new cross-border clash. Commentary and anniversary coverage were not scored; risk holds 15/elevated

dashboard_trackers.name: PAKISTAN-AFGHANISTAN
dashboard_trackers.notes: Past-24h indexes produced humanitarian/context reporting but no independently corroborated new cross-border strike, clash or force buildup. Risk holds 46/critical

dashboard_trackers.name: RUSSIA-UKRAINE
dashboard_trackers.notes: AP reported Aug 6 that Ukraine struck refineries in Bashkortostan and Yaroslavl and said it also hit Russian patrol boats and shadow-fleet vessels; AP separately reported Russia fired four missiles and 101 long-range drones overnight, while NATO chief Mark Rutte was coordinating urgent interceptor sourcing. This reinforces the high-intensity war baseline but does not meet a new configured signal threshold

dashboard_trackers.name: RUSSIA-NATO
dashboard_trackers.notes: No new Article 4/5 action, direct NATO-Russia exchange or configured official nuclear threshold surfaced. The 30 Jul Russian missile impact in Poland remains the key allied-territory event; raw/coupled risk holds 70/80

dashboard_trackers.name: CHINA-TAIWAN
dashboard_trackers.notes: No fresh PLA blockade, invasion or armed clash was verified. North Korea's confirmed short-range ballistic-missile launch raises the configured spillover from 4 to 5 points; China's evidence-based raw probability holds 24 while the coupled dashboard probability moves 28→29 (CRITICAL)

dashboard_trackers.name: DPRK
dashboard_trackers.notes: Reuters, AP and Yonhap confirm North Korea launched at least one short-range ballistic missile from Wonsan toward the sea east of the Korean Peninsula on Aug. 6, its first ballistic launch since late June and shortly before expected U.S.-ROK exercises. The canonical missile_range_test signal activates; raw risk rises 18→24 (ELEVATED). No nuclear test, ICBM launch, impact in Japan or strike on another state was reported

dashboard_trackers.name: SUDAN
dashboard_trackers.notes: Past-24h review surfaced civil-war analysis and civilian-governance advocacy but no distinct new configured buildup, infrastructure-strike or external-intervention threshold beyond the already severe war. Risk holds 94/imminent

dashboard_trackers.name: ISRAEL PALESTINE
dashboard_trackers.notes: UNICEF/OCHA document continuing attacks during the Gaza ceasefire. Reuters/AP now report Uganda approved conditional participation in the proposed International Stabilization Force, with Morocco also pledged; no deployment date exists and the plan remains stalled. ceasefire_violation and diplomacy_active are both active; the evidence-based near-ceiling probability holds 98/imminent

dashboard_trackers.name: SOUTH SUDAN ABYEI
dashboard_trackers.notes: The UN Security Council heard fresh warnings of institutional collapse, famine risk in four counties, deadly cholera and attacks on aid workers as the political settlement frays. This materially worsens humanitarian and political context but does not independently verify a new configured military_buildup, ceasefire_violation or diplomacy_refused event. Risk holds 19/elevated

dashboard_trackers.name: EASTERN DRC
dashboard_trackers.notes: Critical Threats Project reported on Aug. 6 that the Congolese government announced an agreement with the FDLR for voluntary disarmament and demobilization, a concrete implementation step linked to the Washington peace process. The same analysis warns Kinshasa is still deepening collaboration with the group, so this is fragile process evidence rather than conflict resolution. The canonical diplomacy_active signal activates and raw/coupled risk eases 56→53, remaining imminent

dashboard_trackers.name: YEMEN RED SEA
dashboard_trackers.notes: Lloyd’s List Intelligence reported Bab el-Mandeb traffic fell 24% after the Houthi Saudi-shipping blockade and mainstream tanker transits fell 42%; the Joint War Committee expanded the listed war-risk area northward. Saudi Arabia’s 14-country maritime coalition is not yet changing insurer or shipowner risk calculations. Existing ceasefire_violation and infrastructure_strike signals remain active; risk holds at the 100 ceiling

dashboard_trackers.name: MALI SAHEL
dashboard_trackers.notes: Past-24h review found no distinct new attack, deployment or foreign-support delivery beyond older context. The prior foreign-support indicator aged out under the configured 168-hour rule; risk holds 43/critical

dashboard_trackers.name: SOUTH CHINA SEA
dashboard_trackers.notes: Past-24h reporting was analysis of existing China-Philippines pressure and Taiwan-adjacent drills; no new collision, boarding, armed exchange or qualifying buildup was verified. Risk holds 35/critical

dashboard_trackers.name: SOMALIA GULF OF ADEN
dashboard_trackers.notes: The only fresh indexed item was an uncorroborated commentary about a Pakistan-Somalia defence pact. No new UKMTO/JMIC piracy incident or configured threshold was verified; risk holds 28/critical

dashboard_trackers.name: SOUTHERN THAILAND
dashboard_trackers.notes: A local report says security forces conducted an operation against suspects linked to the 22 Jul Narathiwat checkpoint attack. Without independent corroboration or evidence of a broader force buildup, no signal was activated; risk holds 30/critical

dashboard_trackers.name: KUWAIT IRAQ BORDER
dashboard_trackers.notes: Past-24h RSS returned no fresh Kuwait-Iraq border-drone incident. Earlier hostile-drone spillover remains the baseline context; no configured signal changed and risk holds 30/critical

dashboard_trackers.name: IRAQ INTERNAL CONFLICT
dashboard_trackers.notes: Reporting focused on Baghdad pressure to rein in Iran-aligned factions before a September deadline. No new independently verified militia strike or external attack crossed a configured threshold; risk holds 40/critical

dashboard_trackers.name: KENYA SOMALIA BORDER
dashboard_trackers.notes: Past-24h review found AUSSOM and al-Shabaab context but no independently corroborated new Kenya-Somalia border attack cluster or buildup. Risk holds 25/critical

dashboard_trackers.name: EGYPT MEDITERRANEAN
dashboard_trackers.notes: Regional reporting says operations resumed at Damietta after the earlier drone attack. No fresh Mediterranean strike was verified and no canonical de-escalatory signal applies; risk holds 20/elevated

dashboard_trackers.name: SPAIN MOROCCO CEUTA
dashboard_trackers.notes: Middle East Eye reported the Ceuta migrant-disaster death toll had risen to 141, while most entrants had already returned to Morocco. The humanitarian toll rose, but no new military buildup or Spain-Morocco interstate kinetic threshold emerged; risk holds 22/elevated

dashboard_trackers.name: ETHIOPIA TIGRAY
dashboard_trackers.notes: Critical Threats Project assessed the Aug. 1 western-Tigray fighting as major but thus far limited, with artillery/drone use reported. It found no further clashes after Aug. 1, but said neither side relaxed its posture: ENDF reinforcements/checkpoints and separate ENDF/TPLF mobilization near Alamata continue. The older renewed_clashes instance remains decayed; force_mobilization and peace_framework_breakdown remain active. Risk holds 32/critical

allied_positions.red_sea_coalition: Saudi Arabia’s proposed 14-country maritime defence coalition includes Bahrain, Bangladesh, Comoros, Djibouti, Egypt, Jordan, Kuwait, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, Sudan, Turkey and Yemen’s government. The U.S. and EU are absent; Lloyd’s says it is not yet changing insurer or shipowner risk calculations.
allied_positions.gulf_states: Oman, Qatar and other Gulf mediators continue pursuing a Hormuz framework, but fee, sanctions, insurance and traffic-control terms remain unresolved and normal transit has not returned.
allied_positions.gaza_stabilization_force: Uganda authorized conditional participation and Morocco pledged personnel; no deployment date or completed status-of-forces arrangement was found.
allied_positions.nato: NATO’s official news index shows an Aug. 4 NSATU command change but no new Article 4 or Article 5 action. Allies continue Ukraine support.
allied_positions.japan_south_korea_us: Japan, South Korea and the United States shared monitoring data on North Korea’s Aug. 6 short-range ballistic launch; no follow-on salvo or impact on another state was found.
allied_positions.iaea_un: No newer public Iran safeguards report than GOV/2026/33 (4 June) surfaced. UN reporting continues to document Gaza ceasefire harm and South Sudan institutional/humanitarian deterioration.
